The single dataset record for Torah #186 (edge id 1720) is type 'eitza' — אמונה שהם מאמינים בדברי הצדיק → מופתים — not a bechina. Torah #186 is a short five-sentence teaching (5 lines in the source text) about how the miracles of tzaddikim are revealed through the faith of the believers. The teaching argues by analogy: just as prophecy is given in remez (hint) and understood only retroactively (lemafrea) after fulfillment, so too the tzaddik's words function in the same way — hints understood retroactively. The teaching's bechina structure is built around the structural parallel between the tzaddik's words and prophecy, both sharing the quality of remez-and-retroactive-understanding. All packages are derived entirely from source-text gap analysis since the dataset contains no bechina edges for Torah #186. See torah_186_additions.json for proposed new edges.

packages.label: דִּבְרֵי הַצַּדִּיק וּנְבוּאָה
packages.reason: The teaching's central structural insight is that the tzaddik's words (דברי הצדיק) share the same essential nature as prophecy (נבואה): both are communicated in remez (hint/allusion), both are not understood at the time they are spoken, and both are understood retroactively (lemafrea) only after the reality they hint at has been fulfilled. The teaching does not frame this as tzaddik producing prophecy or prophecy causing the tzaddik's words — it explicitly says 'וְכֵן מָצִינוּ אֵצֶל הַנְּבִיאִים' (and so we find with the prophets), establishing that the two phenomena share the same essential structure. The tzaddik's word IS a kind of prophecy; prophecy IS the paradigm of which the tzaddik's word is the living instance. The three nodes (דברי הצדיק, נבואה, רמז) are all expressions of the same underlying reality: hidden truth embedded in allusive speech that is decoded only after the fact. רמז (hint/allusion) is the shared essential medium — it is both what the tzaddik's words ARE and what prophecy IS. Daniel's sealed words are the explicit example cited, establishing that even the most obscure prophetic hints share this same bechina. All concepts are positive, belonging to the domain of tzaddikim and prophets who communicate divine truth.

bechina_1.formula: structural parallel: 'וְכֵן מָצִינוּ אֵצֶל הַנְּבִיאִים' — 'and so we find with the prophets' — the tzaddik's mode of speech is explicitly equated to the prophets' mode
bechina_1.source_quote: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ אֵצֶל הַנְּבִיאִים, שֶׁבְּעֵת שֶׁאָמַר הַנָּבִיא הַנְּבוּאָה הָיְתָה בְּרֶמֶז

bechina_2.formula: identity statement: 'הָיְתָה בְּרֶמֶז' — the prophecy WAS in hint/allusion — remez is the essential nature of prophecy
bechina_2.source_quote: בְּעֵת שֶׁאָמַר הַנָּבִיא הַנְּבוּאָה הָיְתָה בְּרֶמֶז

packages.label: אֱמוּנָה בַּצַּדִּיק וְמוֹפְתִים
packages.label_en: Faith in the Tzaddik and Miracles
packages.reason: אמונה שהם מאמינים בדברי הצדיק (the faith of the believers in the tzaddik's words) and מופתים (miracles) are presented in the opening of the teaching as a pair whose relationship the teaching seeks to explain. The edge in the dataset (id 1720) classifies this as eitza — faith PRODUCES the revelation of miracles — which is correct for the causal direction. However, examining the teaching more closely, there is also a bechina dimension: the teaching states 'כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַצַּדִּיק בְּוַדַּאי מָלֵא מוֹפְתִים' (for in truth the tzaddik is certainly full of miracles) — this establishes that the tzaddik's nature IS miracle: he does not produce miracles from outside himself, he IS full of miracles. The faith does not create the miracles (they pre-exist in the tzaddik); faith REVEALS what is already there. The אמונה and the מופתים are both expressions of the same hidden reality that is already present in the tzaddik. This note documents the bechina dimension: צדיק (tzaddik) shares essential nature with מלא מופתים (fullness of miracles) — the tzaddik IS the miraculous. However, since the dataset edge 1720 already captures the eitza relationship between אמונה and מופתים, and the bechina of צדיק = מלא מופתים is the more precise statement of the teaching, this package is proposed to capture the bechina side. Polarity: good.

merge_notes.note: The dataset edge 1720 captures the eitza relationship אמונה → מופתים. This package proposes the bechina dimension: צדיק = מלא מופתים (the tzaddik's essential nature is to be full of miracles). The concept אמונה belongs in the eitza flow (it is the cause that reveals, not a parallel expression of the same thing as מופתים). The bechina proposed here is narrower and more precise: the tzaddik himself shares essential nature with the miraculous.

stats.good_evil_mirror: Torah #186 does not employ an explicit good/evil mirror structure. The teaching is entirely in the positive domain — it discusses the tzaddikim, the prophets, and Daniel as positive figures of hidden-revealed truth. The implicit negative (the person who does NOT believe in the tzaddik, or the generation that cannot understand Daniel's hints yet) is present as a backdrop but is never developed into a named bechina cluster. This is consistent with short aphoristic teachings in Likutay Moharan that present the positive ideal without developing the negative counterpart into a separate package.
stats.eitza_summary: The causal structure of Torah #186 runs: אמונה בדברי הצדיק —eitza→ נִתְגַּלִּין מוֹפְתִים (faith reveals miracles — dataset edge 1720). The additional implicit eitza chain: הצדיק מלא מופתים (the tzaddik is full of miracles — the prior state) → אמונה → הבנה למפרע (retroactive understanding) → גילוי מופתים (revealed miracles). The 'retroactive understanding' (הבנה למפרע) is an eitza-destination, not a bechina-family member.
